items.title: Companies exploiting welfare system by using residents as 'cash cows', BBC finds
items.summary: Agents try to attract people on housing benefit by using social media videos that offer free rooms and holidays.

items.title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia
items.summary: Two men tell of the work they say they have been doing to support Ukrainian intelligence during the war.

items.title: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos
items.summary: In a BBC World Service documentary, the man claims to have played a role in drone attacks on his home soil.

items.title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting
items.summary: The officer was shot in the foot and remains in hospital in a stable condition, police say.

items.title: Possible wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane likely to be trees, say researchers
items.summary: Researchers travelled to a remote Pacific Island to confirm whether an object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the mystery of the pilot's disappearance.

items.title: Reform MSP quits party to sit as independent
items.summary: Amanda Bland's decision relegates the party to the third-largest group at Holyrood, with one member fewer than Labour.

items.title: Israeli police arrest 10 over settler attacks on journalist and diplomats in West Bank
items.summary: It comes after masked settlers attacked Palestinians and European officials visiting the West Bank during olive harvesting season.

items.title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day
items.summary: More property asking prices are being cut than at any time in 15 years, data shared with the BBC shows.
